svg.title: Blob Fee Market: Demand, Excess Blob Gas, and Reserve Pricing
svg.desc: Rollup batches are published in blob-carrying transactions that pay both execution gas and blob gas. Blob gas usage relative to target updates an excess-usage accumulator, which sets the blob base fee. Fusaka activated PeerDAS, BPO parameter scaling, and EIP-7918 reserve-price behavior linking a minimum blob-fee signal to execution cost.
svg.text: BLOB FEE MARKET
A separate data-space price signal for rollup publishing
EIP-4844 → FUSAKA
1 · Rollup batcher publishes data
Compressed L2 inputs are packaged into a type-3 blob-carrying transaction.
Execution gas · transaction processing / validation
Blob gas · data-space resource priced in a separate fee market
2A · Ordinary execution fee
Execution base fee + any priority fee
Depends on ordinary execution-gas usage
Can be high even when the blob base fee is low.
2B · Blob fee market
Blob gas consumed × blob base fee
Price responds to sustained data-space demand
Blob fee and execution fee are separate charges.
3 · Excess blob gas accumulator
Usage above target builds pressure; sustained below-target usage lets
excess decline toward zero. The protocol computes the next blob base fee.
4 · Fusaka: PeerDAS + BPO + EIP-7918
PeerDAS supports higher data capacity; BPO forks adjust active blob parameters.
EIP-7918 adds a reserve-price relationship tied to execution costs.
Rollup response
compress data · batch efficiently · monitor the active schedule · preserve required DA
Target ≠ maximum. Blob pricing changes over time; do not hard-code old capacity or fee parameters.
